Bringing in our Meta ads specialist for landing-page feedback gives the owner another way to examine the experience while the campaign gathers more data.

reels.spoken_opening: What can we review while a campaign gathers more data?
reels.script:
What can we review while a campaign gathers more data?

In office hours, our Google Ads lead was looking at how much traffic there was to assess and what visitors were doing after they clicked.

Those are different questions, and they help us make a more useful recommendation.

She wanted to give the campaign more breathing room, and she also recommended getting our Meta ads specialist's feedback on the landing page.

That's an approach worth paying attention to when you're deciding what to keep running for your venue.

More time can help us assess how a campaign is performing. A page review gives us another way to examine the experience after the click, including the path to the inquiry form.

We can use both to guide the next decision.

We want enough evidence to make a useful recommendation, and we want the owner to understand what we're looking at along the way.

slides.job: Introduce the perspective and connect it to the venue owner's decision.
slides.text:
Patience and a closer review can work together.

When you're investing in ads to bring more couples to your venue, you want to know what to keep running and what deserves another look. A recommendation to gather more data can also include a useful next step.

slides.job: Ground the principle in Carmen's office-hours guidance.
slides.text:
In office hours, our Google Ads lead considered how much traffic there was to assess alongside what visitors were doing after the click.

She wanted to give the campaign more breathing room. She also recommended getting our Meta ads specialist's feedback on the landing page. Both were part of her guidance.

slides.job: Explain why traffic matters to the timing of a decision.
slides.text:
A campaign needs an opportunity to show us how it's performing.

We consider how much traffic there is to assess before recommending a change. The number of days since launch doesn't tell us how many people have actually visited the page. That distinction matters when we're deciding whether to keep gathering data.

slides.job: Preserve the Google Ads lead's own experience without making an industry-wide claim.
slides.text:
Visitor behavior helps our Google Ads lead decide where to look.

In her work, visits lasting only a few seconds signal that something's off with the ads. When visitors spend time exploring but stop short of an inquiry, she looks more closely at what happens on the page. Those patterns give her different questions to investigate.

slides.job: Show the value of bringing in the right specialist.
slides.text:
Another set of eyes can be a useful next step.

Our Google Ads lead recommended asking our Meta ads specialist for landing-page feedback. That brings another perspective to the experience after the click. The recommendation gives the owner a specific part of the campaign to put forward for review.

slides.job: Explain how evidence gathering and page review fit together.
slides.text:
The campaign can gather more traffic while the page gets a closer look.

One gives us more information about performance. The other helps us examine the experience a visitor encounters before inquiring. Together, they give us more to work with when we consider the next change.

slides.job: Close on what this demonstrates about WIA's support.
slides.text:
Expert guidance includes knowing what to examine next.

We want our recommendations to help you understand what we're considering and why. Sometimes that means giving a campaign more room to run while bringing a teammate into the review. That's the judgment we bring to the conversation.

email.preview: How our team pairs evidence gathering with a useful next step.
email.opening:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

A useful campaign review can leave you with two recommendations at once: give the campaign more time, and take a closer look at the landing page.
email.body:
That combination came up in office hours with our Google Ads lead. She considered how much traffic there was to assess alongside what visitors were doing after the click, then recommended getting our Meta ads specialist's feedback on the page.

For venue owners investing in advertising to reach more couples, that distinction is useful. You want to know what to keep running and where another look could help guide your next decision.

We consider the opportunity a campaign has had to show us something. Days since launch and the amount of traffic available tell us different things, so we look at the traffic before recommending a change.

Visitor behavior adds another perspective. In our Google Ads lead's work, visits lasting only a few seconds signal that something's off with the ads. When visitors spend time exploring but stop short of an inquiry, she looks more closely at what happens on the page.

Those observations help her decide what to examine next. Bringing in our Meta ads specialist for feedback adds another way to review the experience between clicking an ad and completing the inquiry form.

Gathering more data and asking for that feedback can happen alongside each other. We want enough information to make a useful recommendation, and we want the owner to understand the reasoning behind it.
email.ending:
That's part of the value of having experts in the conversation: a clearer view of what deserves time, what deserves attention and where another perspective can help.

Talk soon,
Daniela & Whitney

caption.hook: A landing-page review can be useful while a campaign keeps gathering data.
caption.body:
When you're investing in advertising for your venue, you want a clear sense of what to keep running and what deserves attention. The timing of a campaign change is part of that conversation, and so is the experience people encounter after they click.

In office hours, our Google Ads lead considered those questions together. She wanted to give the campaign more breathing room and recommended asking our Meta ads specialist for feedback on the landing page.

The traffic helps us assess what the campaign has had an opportunity to do. Visitor behavior gives us another way to decide where a closer look could be useful.

In our Google Ads lead's work, people leaving after only a few seconds signals that something's off with the ads. People spending time exploring and then stopping short of an inquiry prompts a closer look at the page.

That reasoning helps shape a useful next step. The campaign can continue gathering data while the owner requests another perspective on the path to the inquiry form.

For a venue owner, expert support includes understanding why we're recommending more time and what we want to examine along the way.
caption.ending: We want every recommendation to give you a clearer view of the next decision.

before_publishing.text: Approve the anonymized office-hours account. Copy omits the client's figures and specific visitor path because recorded permission was not supplied.
The source campaign promoted corporate events at a venue. Do not describe it as a wedding campaign or its visitors as couples.
Do not imply Jacqueline reviewed the page, changes were implemented, a cause was established or results improved.
Keep reported metrics out of the assets. Do not turn Carmen's preferred click count into a universal assessment threshold.
Confirm no explicit ask at Gate 2, and set the email's Tuesday send date, time and recipient segment.
